title: Quiz: what is the price of theta? (hint: another Greek)
summary: A short quiz. The speaker asks what the price of theta is, hints that the answer is another one of the Greeks, and says knowing it puts you ahead of 90-95% of option traders. He leaves the answer to the comments. The chart puts theta next to the other Greeks of an at-the-money call so you can work out the answer yourself.

steps.caption: The clip's question: what is the price of theta? Here, an at-the-money call two weeks from expiry.
Theta: the value the option loses each day. The hint says its price is another Greek.
Candidate one: delta, how much the option moves per $1 in the stock.
Candidate two: vega, how much the option moves per point of implied volatility.
Candidate three: gamma, how fast delta changes. Note it peaks at the strike, where theta is largest.

takeaways: The speaker asks: what is the price of theta?
His hint is that the answer is another one of the Greeks.
He says knowing the answer puts you ahead of 90-95% of option traders, but leaves the answer to the comments.
caveats: The clip only asks the question and never states the answer.
Added context, not from the clip: the usual answer is gamma (option buyers pay theta to hold gamma; sellers collect theta for being short gamma).
